# Agentic Rigg 1.5.0 · build 25

The first open-source release (MIT). This release adds ten interface languages, the Tasks page and card lighting for the Palit RTX 2080 Super JetStream. The local RGB preview has been removed, and the root helpers have a new, verified system installation.

## New

- **10 languages.** The whole interface, notifications, the tray menu and reports are available in Norwegian Bokmål, English, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), Italian, Polish, Simplified Chinese and Japanese.
  - By default the app follows your system language. You can change it under *Settings › General › Language*; the window restarts to apply it.
  - Numbers, dates and times follow the language.
  - The translations were made and cross-checked by AI models. Corrections from native speakers are welcome.
- **Tasks.** A new page lists Linux processes with CPU, memory (RSS) and GPU memory, with search, sorting and a process tree.
  - You can end one selected process after confirming. The app sends SIGTERM via pidfd; system and session processes and the app itself are protected.
  - Pausing keeps the same snapshot while you search, sort and page.
  - `Ctrl+Shift+Esc` opens the page.
- **Card lighting** for the Palit GeForce RTX 2080 Super JetStream: static colour, off, brightness, breathing, rainbow and colour cycle.
  - Changes use the same *Apply* and *Keep* flow as GPU control, with automatic rollback.
  - The helper restores a starting point that you confirmed by looking at the card.
  - Recovery and uninstall work after interruptions and restarts.
- **CPU hotplug.** Sensors, Processor and the sidebar follow changed CPU IDs, also when the thread count stays the same.

## Removed: everything that was only a demo

- The local 2D/3D light model is gone, along with its saved light settings, the "3D card" setting and the easter egg tied to it. The RGB page now shows only what your card can actually do, or a clear message if it has no supported controller.
- The localhost web demo is no longer part of the repository.

## Security: new system installation for GPU control and RGB

- **Verified installation.** The root helpers are installed with one administrator command, which the app shows with a copy button. The command copies the release archive into a root-owned directory and checks it against the SHA-256 you paste from this page before running anything. Nothing in your home directory runs as root.
- **Fixed polkit entry points.** Each enable or disable asks for the administrator password; the approval is not remembered. Admin-side I2C steps run in the same systemd sandbox as the RGB worker, limited to the one identified device. Helpers reject requests with duplicate fields.
- **GPU control must be enabled again once.** The NVML protocol is still version 2, but the oldest accepted helper build is now 25. After updating, install the system components, then turn GPU control on again in *Settings › GPU control*. RGB has its own protocol, version 2.
- Removal: `sudo /usr/local/libexec/agentic-rigg-system/system-install --uninstall` (after turning both helpers off), then `./uninstall.sh`.

## Platform and installation

The target platform is **Ubuntu 26.04 · amd64 · GTK ≥ 4.22 · glibc ≥ 2.39**. System libraries are not bundled. Download the archive and `SHA256SUMS` into the same folder, then run:

```sh
sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS
tar -xzf agentic-rigg-1.5.0-build25-ubuntu26.04-amd64.tar.gz
cd agentic-rigg-1.5.0
./install.sh --bin-dir "$PWD/bin"
~/.local/bin/agentic-rigg
```

Run this as your normal user. Your settings and history are kept. The user install does not activate any helper.

## Verification and limits

- **Automated checks:** Clippy is clean, and the workspace tests pass. The translation catalogs are complete in all ten languages, and an audit for untranslated text passes.
- **Simulated GTK flows:** these were checked in private sessions with a simulated card and a fake RGB worker:
  - GPU control (draft, Apply, Keep, Roll back)
  - the RGB flow with all three effects
  - the language switch
- **Real hardware:**
  - GPU control was verified on an RTX 2080 in 1.4.0.
  - On the Palit RTX 2080 Super JetStream, a static blue and the automatic return to the original green were confirmed by eye.
  - The animated effects, the new system installation and the systemd sandbox for admin steps have not yet run on real hardware.
- **Not implemented:**
  - AMD and Intel GPU backends.
  - RGB on any controller other than the Palit 100.
